title: Museum-vitrine altar still-life -- geometry-signals stress test (2026-08-30)
//: One-off comparison instrument, not a standing census scenario. The prompt is the user's five-element altar stress test, previously run interactively through the GUI (trajectory 20260830T170134Z-75b8b2fa, gemini-3.7-flash): each element quietly demands a shipped geometry signal -- (1) SDF/skeleton guardian: curv edge wear + occlusion patina (the add_wear sweet spot); (2) CSG-subtraction plinth: grime IN the carvings; (3) thin-walled lantern: thickness-driven translucency; (4) three scaled copies of one geometry: curv instancing invariance; (5) lathe goblet: mesh-family bake path. The rerun measures whether the 2026-08-30 hardening (specific expression-compile diagnostics through the finalize sink a71313e4, kind-changed re-land disclosure 2073484d/4d603822, sdf part <a b c> descriptor + degenerate-shape warning 989bfb08) changes agent behaviour: in the GUI run, opaque rejections silently flattened the guardian/plinth expression painters inside build_element's retry, and a box-extents-in-scale-slot slip produced a degenerate plinth SDF. Checkpoints are the generic adoption battery from rich_material_closeup (widened chunk_count for a 5-element scene, same render/diagnostics/trajectory shape); grading of the five elements is post-hoc over the trajectory + final scene, not checkpoint-gated.
prompts:
Build me a small altar still-life, lit like a museum vitrine at dusk:

- A weathered bronze guardian figurine as the hero -- a creature with a rounded body, tapering limbs and a horned head. Centuries of handling: the raised edges and horn tips rubbed back to bright polished metal, dark green-brown patina and grime settled deep into every fold, seam and recess of the casting.
- It stands on a carved stone plinth with recessed panels and chiseled grooves cut into each face -- dust and soot collected in the carvings, the flat faces and outer edges swept clean.
- Beside it, a thin-walled porcelain lantern glowing from a small warm light inside -- the walls should read translucent where they're thin, with the glow dying out where the porcelain thickens toward the base.
- In front, a procession of three identical smaller copies of the guardian at three different sizes, same worn-bronze look on all three -- the wear should sit in the same places on each regardless of size.
- One turned wooden goblet, lathe-profile silhouette, its rim and foot edges worn pale through the dark finish.

Macro camera, shallow depth of staging, one key light plus the lantern. Render and show me.
